NKE.rationale: NKE is a deteriorating business with collapsing profitability, no near-term catalyst, and a valuation that remains expensive relative to its actual earnings power. The Q3 FY2026 results (Feb 2026) show EPS of $0.35, down 35% YoY from $0.54, with operating income of $650M vs $844M a year ago. Revenue is essentially flat YoY (+0.1%) but operating margin has compressed to ~5.8% from ~7.5%. Operating cash flow collapsed 76% YoY to $430M. The stock has declined 25% in the last quarter alone, from $58 to $43.62, yet still trades at 28.7x diluted PE — expensive for a company with negative earnings trajectory, 4.8% net margins, and 16% ROE (down from 32% a year ago). News sentiment is deeply negative (mean -0.37 over 90 days) with multiple analyst downgrades, legal overhang from tariff refund lawsuits, EEOC DEI investigations, and Wells Fargo downgrading to Equal Weight citing weak athletic footwear demand and GLP-1 driven spending shifts. The 'Win Now' turnaround under CEO Elliott Hill is mid-repair with no evidence of margin stabilization — Q3 showed further deterioration from Q2. The Q4 FY2026 earnings call is scheduled June 30, but there is no credible near-term fundamental catalyst; the most likely outcome is continued pressure. Tariff headwinds, elevated promotions, inventory cleanup, and competition from Deckers (HOKA), On, and Adidas all weigh on the outlook. The stock is not cheap enough at 28.7x PE for a business in structural decline with no earnings.
